industry.why: Underweight, from Neutral, on the special topic 'The Sector Memo on telecoms relative strength: pullback or structurally impaired?': the group's relative-strength uptrend has broken on every pre-set measure (all 32 stocks, the median stock, breadth, and the group without its two satellite operators) while 2027 estimates held, so the fall is a de-rating of a leveraged defensive (median two-year-forward price-to-earnings multiple down 12% from end-May to end-September), the pattern that moved Defence last week; the memo's own odds give about one in five that the uptrend resumes by mid-February 2027 and one in four that Industry relative strength is back above 50 by end-January. Component 1 regime, 6-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its high, now present in Europe's own prices: the STOXX Europe 600 0.9% from its 52-week high with the share of stocks above the 100, 150 and 200-day averages at or below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows, breadth recovering for a second week; the causes, inflation, rates, yields, credit and the consumer, unread this week because the strategist and newsletter files did not reach the pack, so the credit-and-cost-of-debt read of 30-Oct-26 with the US ten-year above 5% is held one week stale; sources present 2026-W45, headline-only). Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-11-06 against 2026-09-04, not week on week: F now, D prior, agrees; over the same base the market chose healthcare (A from C) and staples (C from D) as its defensives, not the leveraged one. The sector row C.1 carries the same letter; Towers (D.3), already Underweight, shares the yield leg. No Pool name and no live holding sits here (the Pool's sector relative-strength floor keeps telecoms out), so the Lists are unmoved this week. One notch, not two, because the base rate of 113 past group cases in this position has 55% back above the 200-day average within 26 weeks with a median of +2%, and no lower low has printed. Counter-case: a yield defensive rallies first if the US ten-year falls under 4.5%, and the November results (Vodafone 10-Nov, Telefonica 12-Nov) may show stable churn and pricing. Back to C on Industry relative strength above 30 by end-January with those results stable, or the ten-year under 4.5%; to F on a lower low, or churn and price cuts attributed to switching tools or satellites.

memo.verdict: Progress to Early-Stage Assessment, low-to-medium conviction, with named monitoring triggers carried forward into Section E. This is a narrow progress case, not a clean pass [C]: United Internet clears the Triaging bar on change-force intensity (Element E1, grade B) and a sell-side-corroborated sum-of-the-parts discount (part of Element E8's setup logic), but carries the weakest technical picture (MR1, D) and the worst case-simplicity grade (Element E7, D) of any peer reviewed, cohort or sector. Decision owner: the final decision on progression sits with Richard at Friday review.
case: United Internet clears the Triaging bar on two grounds. First, change-force intensity (Element E1, grade B) is genuinely high and multi-pronged, not merely guided: capex fell for two consecutive actual, reported years (EUR 775m to EUR 731m), with Deutsche Bank calling the 2026 guidance "a critical catalyst for immediate free cash flow expansion" that "should be taken very well by the market"; the FCF inflection (EUR 47m to EUR 321m) is already visible; the stake increase from 78.32% to 86.46% was executed via actual market purchases and a completed tender offer, not announced intent alone, with only ~1.15% left to a mandatory squeeze-out threshold; and IONOS is genuinely and measurably monetising AI (the AI Phone Receptionist already runs at ~EUR 30 ARPU, nearly double the group's blended EUR 16.80; Deutsche Bank estimates AI could contribute up to 50% of IONOS's incremental revenue by 2026), a stronger showing than cohort peer freenet's AI-suitability grade of C.

Second, the sum-of-the-parts discount is real and sell-side-corroborated, not a Watson invention: three independent sources converge — Deutsche Bank ("the combined value of listed stakes in 1&1 and IONOS structurally exceeds United Internet's current market capitalisation"), Redburn (positioning United Internet as "the most liquid, inexpensive vehicle to gain exposure to IONOS's structural growth," with spin-off as "a primary mechanism to crystallise trapped valuation upside"), and Richard's own March-2026 note (a persistent "15-25%" holdco discount). This is the primary Element E8 fit ("Huge/large change-from-current clearing event in solid quality"), with a genuine, quantified, in-progress mechanism (the stake build toward the squeeze-out threshold) as a secondary route to closing the discount from the opposite direction.

Supporting detail: the subscription base proved resilient through a stagnant German macro backdrop (contracts grew 700,000 overall in 2025 despite rising insolvencies and unemployment); Mail & Media's margin expanded to 37.6% in Q1 2026 and is "valued at near-zero" by the sell-side despite genuine defensive quality; a confirmed, dated CFO transition (Carsten Theurer, ex-Schwarz Group, appointed 1-Jan-25) absorbed the departing Shared Services head's entire remit, signalling deliberate reorganisation; and freenet's own memo independently confirms United Internet's broader, more diversified supplier base gives it "materially more supplier-side optionality" than freenet has.
counter_case: United Internet carries the weakest technical picture and the worst case-simplicity grade of any peer reviewed in this exercise, cohort or sector — this is not incidental colour, it is the memo's own stated headline qualifier on the pass. Element E7 (Required case simplicity guardrails) grades D, the worst grade of any Element in the entire memo: a four-layer holding structure sits over an already-complex, binary-outcome subsidiary (1&1), a second separately-listed subsidiary (IONOS), a wholly-owned near-zero-valued cash generator (Mail & Media), and a stranded legal stub (the 4.71% Kublai/Tele Columbus arbitration claim). RA2 (Perimeter narrowness) grades F outright — "the widest perimeter reviewed in this exercise" — and freenet's own memo independently states United Internet "runs a more complex holding structure... a materially wider perimeter" than freenet's, using it as its own positive comparator. At minimum six largely independent drivers are required for the case to work (1&1's network-build execution, the spectrum-sharing resolution, Vodafone wholesale-cost normalisation, IONOS's AI trajectory, the squeeze-out timeline, and the Kublai arbitration outcome); even generously netting correlated pairs down, four or five genuinely independent drivers remain, still failing the shop's "2 or fewer fulcrum / 4 or fewer key drivers" guardrail that sector peers OTE and Vodafone already breach at 5 drivers each — United Internet adds an entire extra holdco layer on top of a comparable operating-level count that neither sector peer carries.

The technical picture is the weakest of any name reviewed: price sits below both the 50-day and 200-day moving averages near the 52-week low, RS percentile 16 (universe) and 18 (sector) place it in the bottom fifth of both sets, and trailing returns show a sustained, not one-off, drawdown (-12.5% 3m, -19.4% 6m, -13.0% 9m, -3.5% 12m, benchmark-relative).
triggers: What would raise conviction: a dated, committed mechanism to close the sum-of-the-parts discount (spin-off, further squeeze-out, or a market re-rating).

What would argue for parking instead: a second consecutive year of guidance disappointment, or an unfavourable spectrum-sharing ruling that locks in permanently higher Vodafone wholesale costs — either would argue for parking in favour of the cleaner, already-progressing 1&1 case.

Named monitoring triggers to watch before Early-Stage Assessment: (1) a dated spin-off, further squeeze-out, or structural separation announcement — the single strongest positive trigger, addressing both the E8 primary-fit gap and the E7 perimeter-narrowness failure simultaneously; (2) a second consecutive year of guidance disappointment — the single strongest negative trigger, given the "MEDIUM" guidance-credibility read; (3) the BNetzA low-band spectrum-sharing ruling, expected 2026-2027, a binary swing factor on Element E11's demand-side read and the Vodafone wholesale-cost exposure; (4) any shift in sell-side language from "potential" to "planned" on IONOS separation; (5) confirmation or reconciliation of the ownership and voting-control discrepancies flagged in Section F.2 via a primary-source filings check.

Priority ESA actions, in order: build an explicit sum-of-the-parts and look-through valuation bridging 1&1 (86.46%) and IONOS (63.80%) economics against United Internet's own market cap; commission the Leadership Foundations and Risks family reports (neither exists on disk yet); quantify the capital claim on United Internet's own balance sheet from 1&1's funding needs (shareholder loans of EUR 225m in Q1 2026 alone, plus the contingent Versatel earnout) against the parent's own standalone free cash flow; re-run the Element E5 thematic-fit grade once the canonical thematics file refreshes (stale since 16-Apr-26); directly test Richard's own prior conclusion that direct 1&1 exposure is cleaner against everything found since; reconcile the ownership/voting-control discrepancies against a primary source before any figure is treated as load-bearing; track whether FY2026 EBITDA guidance (~EUR 1.45bn) is met.

Key questions for Richard: is there a specific reason to analyse the holdco rather than the direct subsidiary now, given the prior "avoid or underweight" framing; does Richard have a position-size ceiling in mind for the elevated monitoring burden (six largely independent drivers per Element E7), in the way 1&1's own Go-No-Go check flagged a 1-2% sizing ceiling for its comparable load; should ESA treat United Internet and 1&1 as one combined position-sizing decision given the ~86% look-through, or keep them genuinely separate; is there appetite to commission a dedicated valuation deep-dive (Financial Analyst role, Excel-based SOTP model) given the entire E8 fit case rests on a discount this Triaging pass could only describe qualitatively.

Three items explicitly unresolved and carried forward as first-order ESA tasks: whether the sum-of-the-parts discount is closing or structurally permanent (the single largest unresolved question in the memo); how much of United Internet's own standalone cash flow is committed to funding 1&1; whether Richard's own March-2026 "invest directly in 1&1" conclusion still holds against the current, more-consolidated ownership structure.

defs.atr: average true range: each day's high to low, stretched to the previous close on a gap, as a % of the previous close; L5D the last 5 sessions, L1M and L3M the last 30 and 91 calendar days
defs.top_half: a close above the midpoint of the day's high-low range; an up day closes at or above the previous close; days with no range are left out
